[PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
## Consolidated Experience from Similar Tasks
The retrieved experiences all describe failures caused by attempting actions without satisfying their preconditions. Pick-up actions require the target object to be present and within the robot's reach, so the robot must navigate to or verify the object's location before picking. Place actions require the robot to already be holding the target object, so a successful pick-up must be completed first. Movement actions require the intended path to be clear; obstacles can block progress, especially after rotations, so environment feedback should be used to detect blockages and replan. In general, do not assume a skill will succeed; verify state and environment conditions before execution, and recover by replanning when feedback indicates failure.

## Preliminary Thinking
For delivering a green round fruit to the sofa: 1) Locate the fruit and sofa. 2) Navigate to the fruit while checking that the path is clear. 3) Verify the fruit is present and within reach, then execute pick-up. 4) Confirm the robot is holding the fruit. 5) Navigate to the sofa, verifying the path is clear after any rotations and replanning if blocked. 6) Execute the place action only when the robot is holding the fruit and positioned at the sofa. 7) Verify the fruit is placed on the sofa. More generally, before every action, explicitly check its preconditions: object proximity for pick-up, holding state for place, and clear path for movement.
[/PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
